text: Hands-on blacksmithing: pick a recipe at a Weapon Station, feed it raw materials, then physically hammer, carve, etch or sew it with smithing tools. Every ingredient you load adds a number of required hits per tool, and you work the station until each tool's counter is full: it refuses extra hits with a tool that is already done, and refuses to finish while any counter is short. The finished item has a quality grade, stats and socket slots. A second station, the Alloy Forge, lets you invent and name your own metal alloys, which anyone can then use as an ingredient. Material ranks matter Metals and woods unlock as you advance through the matching crafting profession. If a station refuses a material, continue that profession until you reach its required rank.

Invent your own named metal at the Alloy Forge. Place an Alloy Forge (recipe above). Right-click the forge holding ingredients to load them. The forge tracks one Base: only a metal or wood ingredient can fill it. The only catalysts a metal or wood base accepts are crystal ingredients: the gemstones and other crystals listed above. Leather, feather, wool, paper and enchanted dust are not valid alloy catalysts (config.yml:47-51). Forge it. You need at least 2 ingredients total (a base plus at least one catalyst). If the resulting alloy is new, you get a 60-second naming prompt: run /alloy name <NewName> (letters and underscores only; underscores render as spaces). Once named, the alloy is stored server-wide and anyone can use it as a crafting ingredient. Alloy naming prompt 60 seconds Minimum ingredients 21 base + at least 1 catalyst

Command What it does Notes /alloy name <NewName> Names the alloy you just invented at the Alloy Forge, inside a 60-second naming prompt. Names may only contain letters and underscores. Underscores appear as spaces, and the naming prompt is available to every player who reaches it.

sectionTitle: Crafting a weapon or piece of armor
text: The loop at the Weapon Station. Place a Weapon Station. Recipe below. Right-click it. A Select Category menu opens (Armor / Weapons / Bows), then a Select Recipe menu. Pick one: a station can only hold one recipe at a time. Right-click the station while holding each required ingredient to load it in. A recipe asks for ingredient types and counts (e.g. "metal ×4"), so you choose which specific metal or wood to use. Right-click the station while holding each required smithing tool to apply hits. Every ingredient you loaded adds its own number of required hits per tool; an on-screen title tracks current/needed for each. Finish the craft once every ingredient is loaded and every hit is completed. Warning Breaking the station mid-craft cancels the project and drops everything you had already inserted.

What you load into a recipe slot decides the finished item's stats, and how many hits of each tool it demands. Base metals and woods: the only ingredients that can be an alloy's base. In-game item id: GEIGER_COUNTER. Somewhere in the world, at all times, there is a single hidden source of Arcane Radiation. The Arcane Trace Detector senses where it is: hold it and it shows glowing particle rings and starts clicking, faster and faster as you get closer. The moment you claim it, the source vanishes and reappears somewhere else entirely. It is a serverwide loot race: there is only ever one source, and whoever reaches it first gets to collect it. Step 1: Get a detector Everything here is crafted at the Engineer Station. Every craft also gives Engineer profession XP. The recharging step needs no profession, so you can trade or buy the detector and fuel from other players and keep recharging it yourself. Unpowered Trace Detector Engineer Station Arcane Crystal 2 Iron Block 2 → Unpowered Trace Detector Arcane Fuel Engineer Station Arcane Crystal Copper Block 4 → Arcane Fuel 16 Yields 16 fuel per craft. Arcane Trace Detector Engineer Station Unpowered Trace Detector Arcane Fuel → Arcane Trace Detector The same recipe recharges a dead detector: no need to re-craft the base item. Step 2: Hunt Hold the detector in your main hand. Particle rings appear around you and the device begins clicking (only you can hear it). Walk and watch the rings and clicking speed. That is your compass. Within about 20 blocks of the source, it is collected automatically. Your detector then runs out of charge and the source respawns to a new location. Step 3: Read the signal What you see or hear What it means 1 ring Over 1000 blocks away. 2 rings Within 1000 blocks. 3 rings Within 300 blocks. Very dark purple, almost black Near the far edge of range (~2500 blocks). Bright purple ~200 blocks out. Turning white Under 200 blocks: the whiter, the closer. Slow clicking (~1 every 2s) Outer limit of the signal. Rapid clicking (a stream) Almost at the source. Step 4: Recharge and go again Claiming the source turns your detector into an Unpowered Trace Detector: "Your Trace Detector has run out of fuel..." You do not need to re-craft the detector: combine it with a single Arcane Fuel at the Engineer Station to power it back up. You can collect 1 source per rolling 24 hours. FAQ "My detector shows nothing." Check that it's the Arcane Trace Detector and not the greyed-out Unpowered version. If unpowered, recharge it with one Arcane Fuel at the Engineer Station. "Somebody else collected the source before me." That happens: there is only one, and it's a race. It has already relocated, so keep hunting; the reading you get now is completely fresh. "I walked right over the source and nothing happened." You're probably at your limit of 1 claim per rolling 24 hours. The source is untouched and still there for someone else. "Can I keep my detector after claiming?" Yes. It just runs out of charge. One Arcane Fuel at the Engineer Station recharges it to full power, so carry spare fuel.

Archaeology turns a buried ruin into a field collection: listen for a site, sample the soil, establish a camp, uncover connected shapes, brush them free, and record their conservation and interpretation.

Hold a dirty recovered piece and right-click the Archeology Cabinet. Match each stain to the lab tool: Water for Limescale, Brush for Soil or Rust, and Air for Mud. Soil and Mud use the same brown pane, so read the stain name. Empty-handed cabinet clicks do nothing. Make a field sketch with Paper in one hand and the Field Pencil or Feather fallback in the other; alternatively click the sheet onto the pencil in inventory. Sign the drawing. The paper is consumed and the pencil lasts 64 sketches. Take the cleaned piece to the cabinet: in the furnace-style registration window, put the drawing in the top slot and the piece in the fuel slot, then choose Register. Filed pieces open a reading. Classifying a find Each reading question offers three phrases. Suggested tags make a matching option more likely to appear, while guaranteed artifact matches ensure that a fitting option is offered. You still choose the interpretation.

The person establishing the camp becomes its director. Right-click the board for the field book, roster and finds list. Add workers by name: the roster has 18 places including the director and no second page. Only roster members may dig. The camp is not a land claim; the excavation prism is the ruin chunk and its depth bands, separate from the tents. Show limits outlines that volume through terrain for you alone for 12 seconds, visible up to 96 blocks away. Open digs you can direct 1 Roster 18 people Workday 8 successful cutsPer Minecraft day; camp planting and brushing are free

Conservation is rolled when the site is generated, from a centered 40-100 range. Subtract 4 for each stratum below the first and another 10 if the band is disturbed; multiply by the material's survival factor, round, then clamp to 1-100. Digging can only reduce it. A careful dig cannot restore a naturally worn piece. Depth is measured below the chunk's median ground level, not absolute Y. Strata do not provide dates: Epoch is a separate reading. Read weights as relative selection weights The find table does not give final drop percentages: available artifacts are filtered by stratum first. Only Pottery sherd, Ancient sword and Burial can occur in Stratum IV. The deepest layer exists only according to the site's interest chance. Burial is the largest shape at 8-15 cells. Conservation grades Grade id Label Minimum % intact Intact 92 sound Sound 72 worn Worn 48 fragmentary Fragmentary 24 crumbling Crumbling 1

Inside the prism, hold left-click on fill with an excavation tool. Soft clings lead to a ready chime. Release on that chime to lift the intended number of cubes. Releasing early lifts nothing; releasing late lifts more cubes with most tools. A distinct find cling or Stop prompt means the cube contains part of a find. Stop treating it as fill. Removed empty cubes reveal neighboring material traces: only shared faces count, not diagonals. Uncover the shape carefully until every surviving find cube has an air face and the shape drips. Hold right-click with a Brush on a dripping cube for 2 seconds. Looking away pauses progress; looking back resumes it. Brush min(shape size, 6) distinct cubes. Small finds need their whole shape brushed. One item then drops with conservation and provenance. The pick never drops the piece; a find at zero conservation cannot be recovered. Destroyed find cells are gone permanently Digging through a find reduces conservation. An ordinary pick can permanently destroy buried finds before a site is established. Faster mining changes cue timing, not the number of cubes lifted. Every successful profile costs one workday action, even a late heavy cut; tool wear is one durability per cube removed and brush wear one per cube cleared. Unbreaking applies normally.

sectionTitle: 5. Display finds and close the dig
text: Shift-right-click a recovered find on an Item Frame, Glow Item Frame, Armor Stand, Lectern or Shelf support to open its plaque. Ordinary clicking keeps Minecraft's normal hang, rotate and take behavior. Empty supports and ordinary items do nothing. Item Displays and custom display cases are not enabled. When every find is recovered or destroyed, the site exhausts: digging and brushing stop, but the camp and board remain. The director can close the camp from the board to free the one excavation slot. Keep the resulting field book and right-click it later to read the archived field book and finds. Care for your tools Archaeology tools cannot be repaired, enchanted, or used in vanilla crafting. Workshop crafting times are listed in seconds. Era names describe the reading attached to a find; they do not assign a precise calendar date.

Hold a Recovery Compass and walk through likely field areas. Pulses accelerate as you approach a ruin; if they fade, change direction. There is no ruin list or directional needle. On approaching and facing the ruin, watch for the prospecting prompt. Use the Soil Probe or Stone Hoe fallback to right-click dirt, grass, sand, gravel, clay or mud. Stone and furniture do not count. Stay within 2 blocks during each 2-second sample. Take four distinct samples, at least 3 blocks apart. A spot counts only once. Two samples give weak traces; three give a possible site; four confirm it. Confirmation belongs to you and does not claim the site. Hold the Camp Kit or documented Stick fallback, aim into a neighboring chunk, adjust the preview to valid ground, then right-click to plant the camp. Do not plant it in the ruin chunk. One command opens the whole shop. Run /armourshop and pick Armour skins or Item skins. Pick a category. The menu shows the categories available to you. Browse the skins available in that category. Click a skin to apply it. If it needs a scroll, the shop checks your inventory for it and for the first item that matches the skin's base set (e.g. a steel chestplate for a steel-tier skin). Missing either one cancels with an error and a sound: nothing is consumed. Applying a skin consumes exactly 1 scroll and merges the new look onto your item, keeping its stats. To go back, use the free Reset to Default category. It covers leather, iron, steel, abyssalite, mythril, mage and infantry base sets. BirdMessenger sends a written letter to another player's character, carried by a bird over real time: there is no command to learn, just a block to find and a GUI to use. Last modified: 2026-09-11
This feature has no player commands.

Delivery time depends on how far away the recipient's character last was. The bird's flight time is based on the distance from where you sent it to the recipient character's last known location: roughly a quarter of a second per block, floored and capped. Minimum flight time 30 secondseven at zero distance Maximum flight time 10 minutesany distance past ~2,400 blocks Cost Free If the recipient is online and actively playing that exact character when the bird arrives, they get the letter immediately with a message that a bird has landed at their feet. Otherwise your letter waits, for that character to be played, or for that player to log in: with no expiry. You'll be told your letter is waiting rather than delivered. Warning A letter can only be delivered within the same world the recipient character's last location was in. If they're in a different world, the bird can't reach them and your letter bounces back as undeliverable. Note This is a different system from sealed letters (the writable-book item you sign and hand to someone in person). Bird Mail is specifically for sending a letter to a character who isn't there to hand it to directly, and it can also forward a Discord DM notification (without revealing the sender or the letter's contents) if the recipient has linked their account.

Everything here is block and GUI interaction: there is no /mail command. Get a Letter item and write your message in it, same as writing a normal book. Find a bird mailbox and right-click it: standing still, not sneaking. Sneak-right-clicking does nothing. A small "Bird Messenger" window opens with one open slot. Place your letter into it, or shift-click it in. Anything that isn't a Letter is rejected. Closing that window with a valid letter in it opens a "Send letter" screen: a page of player-head icons, one per character (your own characters are filtered out: you can't mail yourself). Click the head of the character you want to send to, then hit Confirm. The letter leaves your inventory immediately and a bird flies off with it. If you close the picker without confirming, you get your letter back. Bird Mailbox Right-click the mailbox to send a written Letter.

Ferment, then optionally distil, then optionally age. 1. Ferment. Place a cauldron over a fire or campfire, fill it with water, then right-click it in your main hand with ingredients to throw them in. Right-click with a clock/watch to read the current cook time. 2. Bottle. Right-click the cauldron with a glass bottle to draw off one brew. 3. Distil (optional). Put the bottle in a Brewing Stand with glowstone dust; it runs the recipe's configured number of distill runs. 4. Age (optional). Build a barrel: vanilla barrels work too, up to 6 brews at once, and right-click it to open. Signs on custom barrels must contain the barrel keyword. 5. Seal (optional). A Sealing Table (a re-skinned Smoker) strips a brew down for selling in shops. 6. Drink. The label always shows quality; the exact alcohol number is hidden but an indicator is shown, and drinking prints a status message.

RPCharacters is who you are on this server. Your roleplay chat, injuries and deaths belong to a character you create, not to your Minecraft account directly. In Survival, you cannot do much of anything until you have one. Last modified: 2026-09-11 Warning With no active character, almost every command is blocked: you can still run /rpcharacter ..., /roll, and the chat-channel commands, and nothing else. Making a character is not optional.

Plain typing talks in-character. Everything else is a command. Whatever you type without a command goes to your default channel, which starts as regular in-character speech (rp). Change your default with /channel <id> (bare /channel shows your current one), and hide or show a channel in your own view with /channeltoggle <id>. Investigation is passive by default, active if you want it faster. Characters can leave 2-10 personal clues around the world, plus every character automatically leaves a subtle racial tell. Clues are found passively over time just by being nearby, or actively by holding a magnifying glass (four tiers exist, better ones see further and find things faster) and right-clicking to search. Clue potency fades over time, so an old clue is harder to read than a fresh one. /rpcharacter clues opens your own clue list.

One command starts a long guided creator: expect to spend real time on this. Type /rpcharacter create to begin. You will be walked stage by stage through: an out-of-character age gate (18+), your character's name (typed in chat), class information and selection, race selection, character age, a set of trait choices (homeland, cataclysm, reclamation, motivation, gift, virtue, combat, physical, celestial), attribute allocation, personality, an optional evil archetype, a permanent injury roll, an optional prosthetic, a written description, an opening clue, and finally your wardrobe. Use /rpcharacter next, back, help and cancel to move through it. Once you have a character, /rpcharacter menu opens a menu of your characters so you can switch between them (on a cooldown: see below), and /rpcharacter kit starter claims your starting supplies: an iron hunting knife, 32 gold coins, 256 bread, a writable book, a bundle and a brown bed. The starter kit can only be claimed once per character, with a 48-hour cooldown. Death and injury are part of the roleplay, not just a stat penalty. Injuries can be healing (temporary) or permanent, and range from a broken arm to full blindness: each comes with real stat penalties while it lasts. Two players can arrange a consensual roleplay injury with /rpcharacter injure <player>: you pick the injury from a GUI, then the target has to confirm it within 30 seconds. If your character dies, a grave chest appears with a hologram showing who killed you: right-click it to recover your things (or let someone else rob it). Graves never expire on their own. A Grave Insurance item, if you have one, recovers your newest grave from anywhere. Seven selectable classes cover different equipment and play styles. They deal sustained damage from a distance, and are excellent at maintaining a favourable position, making them ever-reliable. Cooking has no menu and no crafting table. It is a set of real furniture props you place in the world: a pan, a pot, a cutting board, an oven, a milling stone, a fire pit with a spit, a butter churn, a sausage maker. Put ingredients on them, work the station, and the food item you get back tracks its own freshness, cooked state, seasoning and a 1–5 star quality rating: all shown in the item's name and lore. There is nothing to type; everything is a right-click.

Each right-click with the Cutting Knife on a roast or sausage chain takes one cut off, in this order. Sequence Cuts Yields in order Whole Chicken 6 Chicken Leg ×2, Chicken ×3, then 2 Bone Beef / Venison Roast 8 Beef ×7, then 4 Bone Sausage Chain 5 Sausage ×5
Fire Pit Whole Chicken, Beef Roast, Venison Roast Frying Pan Chicken, Chicken Leg, Steak, Beef, Venison, Pork, Sausage, Cut vegetables Pot Cut vegetables

Every recipe the Cutting Board can run. Recipe Input cut_vegetables Any raw vegetable (Carrot, Potato, Tomato, Onion, Lettuce, Cucumber, Corn, Beetroot, Pumpkin) chop_vegetables Any cut vegetable chop_olive Olive chop_pistachio Pistachio chop_rhubarb Rhubarb chop_garlic Garlic Olive, Pistachio, Rhubarb and Garlic skip the cutting step and go straight to chopped : every other vegetable above is cut first, then optionally chopped again.

The furniture and the two clicks that drive every station. 1. Place the furniture you need: Frying Pan, Pot, Cutting Board, Fire Pit, Milling Stone, Mixing Bowl, Oven Bottom + Oven Top with a Bread Tray, Butter Churn, Sausage Maker, Meat Hook, or a plain vanilla Cauldron. 2. Right-click the furniture while holding an ingredient to place it into one of the furniture's slots. 3. Right-click with an empty hand to take the item back out, or to operate the station (churn, turn the spit, stir). 4. Stations that need heat (the Frying Pan) only cook while a heat source sits underneath: the server's only configured chain is an Oven Bottom (heat source) under an Oven Top. 5. Cooking ticks once per second, so every time listed below is in real seconds, not ticks.

What to hold and what happens at each station. Station Held item / action Result Cutting Board Hold the Cutting Knife and interact Runs a cutting/chopping recipe on up to 4 slots at once: all 4 must be the same ingredient. Frying Pan Place food, needs heat below; take out by hand Cooks over time; burns if left on too long. Pot Add a Water Bucket, then cut vegetables Makes boiled foods and soups. Fire Pit Put a roast on the spit, then right-click with the Fire Pit Turner Rotates and roasts a whole joint (chicken, beef, venison). Meat Hook + Cutting Knife Carve a cooked roast Yields cuts one at a time, in a fixed order. Milling Stone Insert 8 Wheat, then perform 4 revolutions 1 batch of Flour, over 60 ticks (3 s). Mixing Bowl Add Flour + Cup of Water + Yeast, then stir 3 times Dough (10 ticks per stir). Bread Tray (in an Oven) Fill both moulds with Dough, light the oven with logs 2 Bread per mould. Butter Churn Right-click with a Milk Bucket to load it, then repeatedly right-click the stick 3 churns deliver Butter onto a carried Butter Plate. Sausage Maker Feed 3 meats, then crank A Sausage Chain you carve for 5 sausages. Cauldron (vanilla block) Right-click while holding a sauce or soup item Empties/serves the liquid.

CustomCrops replaces vanilla farming with 30 custom crops planted in watered pots. Nothing here is a vanilla crop block: every crop is a small model sitting in a pot, and it only grows while that pot is watered. This is where almost every fruit, vegetable and spice used by Cooking and DrinkBuilder comes from.

'Regrows' means harvesting rolls the plant back to an early stage instead of destroying it, so it keeps producing. Till, water, plant, wait, harvest. 1. Till ground into farmland as normal: pots sit on top of vanilla farmland. 2. Water the pot: right-click it with a water bottle/potion, or fill a Watering Can at water and right-click pots to soak a 3×3 area. Pots also absorb rain and adjacent water on their own. 3. Right-click the watered pot holding the crop's seed item. You need that crop's profession permission, or you're told you can't plant it. 4. Wait. The crop advances a growth stage only while the pot's water is above a threshold. 5. Optionally speed things up with Bone Meal or a fertiliser. 6. Right-click the fully grown crop with an empty hand (or break it) to harvest: you get 2–4 produce plus a seed back.

Games turns any block into a card table. Place a deck, pick a game from a GUI, and bet real denars against other players (or the house) at Blackjack, Tenceur Hold'em, Five-Draw, or a no-rules Free play table. Cards float in front of you as 3-D displays that only nearby players can see, and money actually changes hands: winnings are taxed like any other income.

The only game with a table actually standing on the server today. While betting is open, right-click your own box on the felt holding coins. Click again to add more. When your name comes up, right-click the shoe for a card, or type hit, stand, double, or split in chat. Those words only register on your turn. /games bet hit does the same thing. The dealer reveals and draws to 17. This house does not hit soft 17. A win returns double your bet; a natural 21 on the first two cards pays 3:2; a push returns your bet. No insurance and no surrender are offered. To deal by hand, stand at the dealer's spot and right-click the shoe; right-click again to hand it over. A dealer runs /games bet min <n>, /games bet max <n>, /games bet open, /games bet close, then right-clicks the shoe. Some tables deal themselves : betting opens automatically once the first real bet lands.

Everything else at a table: placing it, dealing, betting coins, drawing, discarding, revealing, taking the free-play pot: is clicks and chat words, not commands. The chat words a table recognises, only on your turn, are hit, stand, double, split, check, call, raise, fold, and draw (Five-Draw stand-pat only). No rules, no turns, no dealer. Right-click the shoe empty-handed for a card. Click cards then right-click the shoe to discard them. No limit on how many you hold. Right-click the felt with coins to add to the middle. Warning Sneak + right-clicking the shoe picks up the entire pot. Play with people you trust.

Tenceur Hold'em and Five-Draw share the same seating and betting flow. Right-click the felt with coins to sit down. Once two players are seated, anyone at the table can right-click the shoe to deal. Bet by pushing coins onto the felt first, then saying the word in chat: check, call, raise, fold. The table reads how many coins you actually put out, so saying "raise" with nothing on the felt does nothing. The dealer button shown above the table moves one seat after every hand; it sets who acts first. Five-Draw only: on your draw turn, click the cards you want to discard, then right-click the shoe for that many replacements. To stand pat, type draw in chat: chat only, there is no /games bet draw. Calling with less than you need puts you in for what you could manage: side pots are created and you can only win what you matched. Walking off forfeits this round's stake; earlier rounds' stakes do not return. Warning The blinds shown above a Hold'em or Five-Draw table are advisory only. Nothing is taken from you automatically: whoever owes a blind has to put the coins out themselves.

Rules shared by every table, whichever game you pick. Cards render fanned in front of you, visible only within 48 blocks. Left-click a card in your fan to inspect it. Press your swap-hands key (F) to flip your whole hand face-up for the table. Right-click the shoe (the deck sitting on the table) to draw, deal, or act. Right-click the felt while holding coins to bet. Walk more than 6 blocks from the table and your cards return. This round's stake comes back with them. Only whole denars go on a table; silver bits are refused. The house's own help book puts it plainly: "Only whole coins go on a table. Silver bits are no good." Winnings are subject to the usual citizen tax, same as any other income.

Place a table and invite other players to join. Hold a Deck of Cards. Right-click a block. A game-select GUI opens with four icons. Pick a game. Blackjack opens a table-options GUI (min bet, max bet, house settings) first; Poker, Five-Draw and Free play arm placement immediately. Click the spot to place the table. Sneaking cancels an armed placement. Picking the table back up drops the Deck of Cards item again at the table's origin.

Betting something other than coins. Hold the item, type /wager <amount>, and the table votes on whether it counts (a 30-second window). If accepted, you have 10 seconds to click the felt with that same item. With only one other player at the table, a wager auto-accepts if nobody else has bought in. Note Place a Deck of Cards to set up a table and choose a game. Note The deck is themed to server lore: the four suits are cerrith, mitlan, oseni and seithr, rather than hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades.

Gathering spots spawn hidden in the wild. Your character notices one when you walk close enough: a message tells you something is nearby, and a faint particle ring marks the spot. Right-click it to harvest whatever loot it rolls.

Passive discovery is rolled once every 12 seconds for everyone within range. Detection range 6 blocks Wisdom bonus +2%per point of Wisdom Intelligence bonus +1.5%per point of Intelligence Herbalism bonus +1%per level of the Herbalism profession

Discovery is tracked per roleplay character, not per account. Spots spawn on their own on eligible blocks, invisible until discovered. Every 12 seconds, every player within 6 blocks of a spot has a chance to notice it. On a success: "You notice something glinting nearby..." A discovered spot shows a small particle ring so you can find it again. Right-click the spot to gather. Loot is rolled and the items pop out with a little velocity. If the roll comes up empty: "Nothing to gather here." The spot is consumed: gathering it once uses it up, and its chunk goes on cooldown.

What you actually get for harvesting a spot. A forest-herbs spot gives 1–2 loot rolls, and every roll currently comes from the same pool: 2–4 Stack of Gold Denars (worth 10 denars each, so 20–40 denars per roll).

Whole map provinces can get overrun by monsters: on this server, every infestation you will meet is swamp-flavoured and shown on the map as "Bog Monsters". Walk into one and it spawns ambient enemies around you on its own; place a Lure and you can fight a single big wave that, if you win, clears the province outright.

What actually happens once you step into an infested province. Walk into an infested province at night. Ambient monsters spawn in a ring around you, up to a cap, on a fixed interval: both scale with severity. To go further, place a Lure. This opens a 20-second join window: leave the province, or right-click the Lure to commit to the fight. If you neither join nor leave, the lure starts without you and you take 2 deserter damage per check for staying nearby uncommitted. Clear every mob and the infestation is cleared outright; dying, running out the timer, or leaving means the infestation remains. Logging out mid-Lure does not save you: there is only a 300-second grace period, after which you are marked to die on your next login. Note Placing a Lure in a clean (non-infested) province does nothing. Only one Lure can be active in a province at a time.

Infestations are province-wide and only active at night. Infested provinces are shown on the server's web map with a severity label. Ambient spawning and Lure waves only happen while it is night in-world: during the day an infested province is quiet.

Two reasons to seek an infestation out rather than avoid it. An infested province is simply more dangerous ground. It keeps spawning monsters around you for as long as you stand in it, at night. That is a steady stream of kills if you want one. Committing to a Lure raises the stakes further: a single scripted wave sized to the province's severity, fought to a clean win-or-lose result, with the province's infestation lifted entirely if you clear it.

Magic is the mage path. You build a staff, wand or blade out of parts at a Magic Station, slot spell runes into it, and then attune it to one of ten elements by feeding it magical energy you gathered from a shrine. Your character also carries a personal Resonance score in every element, and a weapon will simply refuse to fire if your Resonance is too low for what it holds.

Three weapon shapes, each wanting a different set of parts. Archetype In-game name Melee: Parts it needs Staff Mage Staff No Core, Handle, Tome x3 Wand Wand No Core, Handle, Tome Sword Mage Blade Yes Core, Handle, Tome

Hold the weapon, right-click. Three different ways it can go wrong. What you see Why What it costs you *Whiff* Your Rift rolled against you (or the rarer "Too many staffs" message). Mana and the cooldown, both already spent. *Refused* Your Resonance is below what the weapon asks, or the weapon holds no element at all. Nothing. *Damaged* A config change left the weapon holding runes it can no longer seat. Nothing, but the weapon will not cast until you reclaim its runes. A refusal explains itself in chat: "The weapon asks for {element} {need}. You carry {have}.", but only once every 30 seconds per weapon and element, so do not expect a message on every click. To fix a Damaged weapon, right-click an empty Magic Station: it works the loose runes free and hands them back.

A charge is a consumable, not an artifact. Put it on a pedestal in a shrine and it is imprinted with every element that shrine scores, then filled from it. A weak shrine cannot fill a high-tier charge. That is the tier gate. The band printed on a charge ("Cerrith II") is just a readout of how much aura it holds: under 10 shows a dash, 10 is I, 40 is II, 75 is III, 110 is IV.

One command. Everything else is done by touching the world. Command Aliases What it does /resonance /res Opens your Resonance profile: a bar per element, your Equilibrium (Corruption vs Tranquility), your Mental Points, and the Surge / Flow cast-mode toggle.

The intended loop, start to finish. Be a Mage. The Mage class is what gates Mage Staffs, Mage Wands, Mage Blades and Mage Armor. Its own description warns that mages are expensive to gear. Open /resonance and pick a cast mode: Surge ("Power now. Corruption later.") or Flow ("Slow start. Stronger at depth."). Flow is the default. Craft and place a Magic Station, then interact with it to open the assembly menu and build a weapon out of parts. Slot runes into the weapon's sockets. This is where spells come from; a weapon with no runes casts nothing. Build a shrine and put an artifact on a pedestal in it to soak up aura. Imprint and fill a charge on that same pedestal. Spend the charge on the weapon at the station, which starts the orb minigame that decides how much of the charge actually sticks. Hold the weapon and right-click to cast.

Shrines do not only fill artifacts. Standing in one and meditating is how you raise your own Resonance. Resonance per orb hit 4.0 Mental Point cost per hit 1 Mental Point pool 150shared with Research Regeneration +10 / houroffline too Mental Points (also called Focus) are a shared pool spent by both Magic meditation and Research experiments. Wisdom adds +0.5 per hour per point and Intelligence +0.25. A full pool of 150 takes fifteen real hours to refill and buys 150 orb hits. That is 600 potential Resonance before element caps, shared-artifact division and session limits. Resonance bleeds, and artifacts get tired of you Resonance decays at -0.02 per real hour, so a mage who stops meditating slowly slides back. Worse, an artifact you meditate on gets muffled: it gives less and less over 24 hours of use, and takes a full 7 days to recover. If several people are attuned to one artifact, the yield is divided between them. Storing an artifact in a chest raises its muffle, silently. Safe places are your own inventory, a pedestal, an artifact display, or an item frame.

Applying a charge to a weapon does not just write the attunement. It starts a timed minigame, and the charge is spent up front whether you win or not. Orbs circle you. Pale blue orbs are good: hit enough of them before the window closes and the weapon settles, holding a percentage of the charge. Rust-orange orbs tear the weapon: each one you hit adds +5 persistent Rift, capped at 100. Missing a good orb costs 8% of the run. Disconnecting mid-run ends it with whatever you had. A charge can exceed your Resonance Right-click the prepared weapon on its station with the charge to start. If the charge demands more Resonance than you have, the configured warning lists each shortfall and asks you to right-click again to commit anyway. That second click spends the charge. Rift per bad orb +5capped at 100 Rift removed per later recharge 10never on the first charge Rift persists until reduced by a later recharge Rift is the percentage chance a cast simply fails. A failed cast still spends the mana and still starts the cooldown. You can only ever grind it back down 10 points at a time, and only on a later successful charge.

A plain vanilla 3x3 craft. Anyone can make one. Magic Station Crafting Table Requires: None Blackstone Blackstone Blackstone Blackstone Gold Ingot Blackstone Blackstone Amethyst Shard Blackstone → Place it, then interact to open the weapon assembly menu.

Five words you need before anything else makes sense. Term What it means Element One of ten flavours of magic: Cerrith, Oseni, Seithr, Mitlan, Bloodmagic, Spirit, Arcanum, Illusion, Necromancy, Shadowmancy. Resonance A 0-100 score your character holds in each element separately. It decides whether a weapon will accept a charge, and it scales the mana cost, damage and cooldown of your spells. Aura The physical resource. It lives inside artifacts and charges, is gathered from shrines, and is spent to attune a weapon. Aura in an artifact never decays. Socket A hole in a finished weapon that one spell rune fits into. Sockets come in four sizes: Minor, Lesser, Greater and Ascendant, and a rune only fits its own size. Attunement Locking an element into a weapon by spending a charge on it. Until you do, the weapon holds no element and refuses to cast. It is per character, not per account Resonance and Equilibrium are stored against your active RP character. A second character starts from zero. /resonance refuses to open at all without an active character.

Command Aliases What it does Notes /instruments keybinds None Prints the full note and chord layout for the instrument currently in your off-hand. "My instrument makes no sound." Three things, in order. One: your Jukebox/Note Blocks volume slider must not be at zero: notes play in the Records category, not Master or Ambient. Two: the instrument must be in your off-hand. Three: press 1–8; slot 9 is the reset slot and plays nothing. "Can I craft an instrument without being a Bard?" No: all nine recipes require the Bard class. "Can I play an instrument without being a Bard?" Yes. The instrument items carry no class requirement and no stat requirement of any kind, and nothing checks your class when you press a key. Instruments are tradeable, so a non-Bard handed one plays it exactly as well as its maker. "Do I need a permission?" No. Both instrument commands are available to every player.

Put the instrument in your off-hand. Your main hand is irrelevant. Press number keys 1 to 8 to play notes. The scale runs: 1=C, 2=D, 3=E, 4=F, 5=G, 6=A, 7=B, 8=C (an octave up). Hold Shift and press 1 to 8 for the second layer. On most instruments that's a full chord; on the Flute, Trumpet and Bagpipe it's the same scale an octave higher, giving sixteen notes total. After every note your selection snaps back to slot 9. This is deliberate, and lets you hit the same note twice in a row instead of the key doing nothing the second time. Whatever sits in slot 9 is therefore what bystanders see in your main hand while you play. A single note particle appears above your head with each note, so everyone can tell it is you.

The Recycling Station breaks a crafted item back down into a share of the materials it took to make it. A pristine item gives back the most; a worn-down one gives back less, and a fully broken item gives back nothing at all.
Built on a vanilla crafting table. Recycling Station Crafting Table Requires: None Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks →

Right-click the placed station to open it. Right-click the Recycling Station. A 3×9 GUI opens. Drop the item you want to break down into the input slot. An item that cannot be recycled at all is rejected with "That item cannot be recycled here." The middle columns of the GUI preview exactly what you would get back. If recycling it would return nothing, the preview says so and the confirm button is blocked. Click confirm. Your outputs are spawned and kicked out of the station, and you get "Recycling complete." If you close the GUI with an item still sitting in the input slot, it is returned to you.

Three sources are checked, in this order. Source How the return is worked out Weapons and Armor Refunds the exact ingredients (or alloy components) that were used to craft it. Guns Refunds materials according to the weapon recipe and its remaining durability. Items with a dedicated recycling recipe Returns materials from its recycling recipe.
Research is an item-based deduction puzzle. Make a research paper at a Cartography Table, study it at a Lectern, and test materials to uncover and fill its hidden aspects.

Rule Meaning Primary / secondary aspect An item contributes more strongly to each primary aspect than to each secondary aspect. One item can contribute to several aspects. Rejected An aspect outside the hidden recipe is rejected after enough testing. An experiment containing only rejected aspects is blocked. Undiscovered Aspect Its row appears after you make some progress toward the required points. Intelligence makes it appear sooner. Confirmed Its identity appears after further progress. Intelligence makes it appear sooner. Confirmation is not completion: keep filling it. Product reveal The product appears after enough aspects are confirmed. Intelligence can make it appear sooner, but early reveal is not assured. Completion Every hidden aspect must reach its full required points. Total points are not an experiment count, because tests may contribute to multiple aspects. A concrete experiment example Arcane Crystal is a primary Arcane item, so it supplies 2 Arcane points when tested. Crying Obsidian is secondary Arcane and supplies 1. These are distinct items, so each can be tested once. The Arcane Crystal project requires 3 Arcane points, plus its Earth, Energy and Machine requirements.

Maximum Focus 150Stored per RP character; shared with Magic meditation Each experiment 1 point Base refill 10 per real hourRegenerates offline; 15 hours from empty to full Wisdom adds 0.5 points per hour per attribute point; Intelligence adds 0.25. The regeneration interval is one hour. When exhausted, the lectern tells you that you are too tired to research. The aspect table counts distinct primary and secondary items; it is not a recipe or a list of required quantities.

sectionTitle: Make a paper and start a project
text: Sneak-right-click a Cartography Table to open the Research Station. Combine one vanilla Paper and one Alchemy Powder for one Parchment Paper. It takes 5 seconds. Combine one Parchment Paper with the subject ingredient. Ordinary papers take 5 seconds; an Unknown Research Paper takes 15 seconds. Every station recipe grants 10 Herborist EXP. Recipes hide when you lack their ingredients. Hold the resulting paper and right-click a Lectern. Each lectern has one owner, so find another lectern if one is occupied. A Staff Runestone can start its own project without first becoming a paper. Choose an experiment item, inspect its point preview, then confirm. Each different item may be tested once per project. Items with no aspect tags cannot be used. Use the Testing, Confirmed and Rejected labels to guide your next experiment. Fill every required aspect completely, then collect the result that drops above the lectern. It is not placed directly in your inventory. Warning Breaking the lectern destroys the project. The Scrap button also destroys it after a confirmation and does not refund the project.

Thievery is the server's in-house crime system. You can lock your own doors and chests with keys, and you can break into other people's doors, chests, display furniture and graves with lockpicks, pickpocket players, or hold someone up in a consensual timed robbery. Almost everything you do here can leave a clue pointing back at your character.

Command Aliases What it does Notes /thievery None Lists the player subcommands (loadout, clearclues). Use the subcommands below to manage your loadout and activities. /thievery loadout None Opens the 30-point steal-category loadout GUI. Requires the "thief" character trait, else you are told you lack the needed trait(s). /thievery clearclues None Arms a right-click to wipe clues from one door or container. No permission check exists in the code for this command. /pickpocket None Shows pickpocket usage. None /pickpocket start None Arms a right-click to pickpocket a player within 4 blocks. Requires the "thief" trait. /robbery None Shows robbery usage. None /robbery start None Arms a right-click to demand a robbery from a player within 4 blocks. Requires the "bandit" trait. /robbery accept None Accepts a robbery demand aimed at you. No trait or permission needed: any player can accept.

Copying a key costs no crafting bench, just your own inventory. Drag one item onto another directly in your inventory: Copying a key to paper is on a 240-minute (4 hour) per-player, per-key cooldown. Pick up (cursor) Click onto Result Clay Ball a master key Key Mold Copper Ingot a key mold Copper Key (permanent) Paper a master key or copper copy Paper Key (single-use, doors only)

Protecting your own doors and containers. Doors: hold a key (Iron Key or Gold Key) and sneak + right-click the door to lock it. Sneak + right-click again with the same key to unlock it; a wrong key is rejected. While locked, a door will not open (and cannot be broken) without the matching key. Containers: you automatically own any container you place. Sneak + left-click a container you own to cycle its lock state: Private → Guild → Public → back to Private. Ender chests are excluded from the whole system.

The offensive loop: breaking into someone else's stuff. Hold a lockpick (only one exists on this server: the Basic Lockpick Set) and right-click a closed, locked door within 3 blocks: or a lockable container, display furniture (artifact display, pedestal), or entity (armor stand, item frame, glow item frame). Doing this requires the "thief" character trait; without it you are told you lack the needed trait(s). A minigame starts: a 20-slot bar scrolls alongside your current risk. Right-click the door/container again to strike: land on a success slot (up to 3 wide) and avoid the break slots. Doors that are successfully picked enter a 60-minute unlock window during which anyone can open them. Containers and furniture do not hand you the contents directly on a success: you get a Steal GUI instead. You click slots to probe them; each probe risks breaking your lockpick, and each item you take costs budget points from your loadout. Graves work the same way as containers: right-clicking another player's grave opens the Steal GUI with a 10-point budget.

Taking directly from another player. Pickpocketing: /pickpocket start, then right-click a target within 4 blocks. A Steal GUI of their inventory opens with a 10-point budget. The victim sees a warning subtitle (a rarer "critical" version names your character directly). Moving too far away ends it. Robbery is opt-in: /robbery start on a target, who must run /robbery accept within 30 seconds or the request times out. Once accepted, the victim is frozen and cannot move; you get 120 seconds and a 30-point budget. Clicking their coin pouch takes 10 denar per click, shift-click 100.

Open /professions and buy Engineer ranks in the Crafter profession. Engineer I costs 1 point for ground vehicles. Engineer II requires I and costs 2 more points for ships. Engineer III requires II and costs 3 more points for aircraft. Craft and place an Engineering Table for land vehicles, fixed guns and aircraft, or a Dockyard for ships. Use the crafting-table patterns below. Right-click the station, choose a category and select a blueprint that your Engineer rank unlocks. Gather its listed materials before selecting the building spot. Left-click the intended spawn point within 12 blocks of the station. Choose it within 30 seconds of selecting the blueprint. The materials are consumed when you choose the spot. Wait for the build to finish. Stay within 96 blocks so the completed vehicle can appear, then right-click it to claim it and select a seat. It takes six minutes to build and carries 54 cargo slots. Warning Breaking the construction station during a build cancels construction and drops the materials at the station. Collect them before they despawn.

Enter: right-click the vehicle and choose a seat. Shift reopens seat selection while aboard. Only the captain steers. Drive: run /vf keybinds while seated to see the controls for your vehicle. W/S commonly adjusts throttle and A/D steers. Controls can change between ground, flight and water. Refuel: hold the fuel listed on the vehicle page and right-click once per item. Each Coal Block or Arcane Fuel adds 100 fuel units. Stop an Arcane Fuel engine before refuelling; Coal Blocks can be added while an engine runs. Carry cargo: right-click a vehicle with storage to open its containers. Wooden Cart and Cloudskimmer each hold 54 slots. Behemoth has four 54-slot holds. Coal Car holds 27 slots of Coal Blocks. Tow: sneak-right-click a Wooden Cart or Field Artillery, then sneak-right-click a Horse Cart to connect it. Repeat on the towing vehicle to detach. Stay within eight blocks while making the connection. Save fuel by stopping the engine Fuel burns at a flat rate while an engine runs at nonzero throttle. A damaged engine also limits maximum throttle, so repair it to restore power.

Claim a new vehicle by right-clicking it. A claimed vehicle starts with an owner-only whitelist. Open Ownership Settings in Select Seat to allow other players, add a player by name or enable passenger tickets. With tickets enabled, hold Paper and right-click your vehicle to make matching tickets for passengers. Reset Owner releases ownership. Clicking an occupied yellow seat ejects its passenger and prevents re-entry for 60 seconds. Use /vf findvehicles to locate your vehicles. Vehicles more than 160 blocks from players unload into storage; they are not destroyed.

Hold Vehicle Repair and right-click a grounded, stationary vehicle, or use a mechanic seat to repair while aboard. Use the Repair Tool in the menu to fix components and the Water Bucket for fires. Keep the menu open and stay nearby until repair finishes. Hold Vehicle Paint and right-click to open Select Skin. Engineer Station tool Materials Time Requirement Vehicle Repair 4 Iron Ingots 5 seconds Vehicle Mechanic profession Vehicle Paint 1 Common Item Skin Scroll 5 seconds Vehicle Mechanic and Gilded rank or higher Vehicle Mechanic costs two Crafter profession points. Keep ship pumps repaired to control flooding. Repair damaged engines and wings to recover performance.

Choose a vehicle above, then select one of its available skins beside the preview. Drag the model to rotate it and scroll to zoom. The vehicle name opens its full materials and specifications page. In game, use Vehicle Paint to choose from the skins available to you.

Build trains on custom train tracks. Craft Train Track in batches of 64 at the Block Station. Leave room for wide bends and gentle slopes: turns have a 35-degree limit, and slopes have a 10-degree maximum.
